newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real falls 0.08 pct under new miniband.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real falls 0.08 pct under new miniband.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.08 percent to close at 1.0535 real per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a new mini-band for the currency, dealers said.
During the morning session, the Central Bank set a new trading level for the real by buying dollars at 1.0535 real per dollar and selling dollars at 1.0585 real per dollar.
Under the previous mini-band, set on March 5, the real was traded between 1.0525 and 1.0575 real per dollar.
In late afternoon trade, the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0535 real per greenback to maintain the trading level within the new mini-band, traders said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Monday surplus of $49.1 million.

In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real also dropped 0.09 percent to end at 1.0586 real per dollar. In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.46 percent to end at 1.080 real per dollar.
